brief: A planter of four cells with a water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell.

requirements.evidence: I placed four full hex bases in a straight row at (0,0), (1,0), (2,0) and (3,0), level 0. Each holds a drained third-depth bin (hex-bin-third-drain). Joint bolts on the three shared walls join the bases into one body.

requirements.requirement: Water pipe running through the bases
requirements.evidence: Pipe run run:run-1 is set to irrigation mode. It enters at the outer edge of (0,0) (entry edge 3) and passes straight through all four bases at level 0.
The run passes through all four cells, and each has a drained bin sitting over it. The configurator only offered third-depth bins in cells the pipe passes through, so the planters are shallow.
check_build: ok, no errors, meshClash "clear". The only note is an info item saying 18 open edge faces could take optional caps.

finish.summary: I built a four-cell planter in a straight row: four full bases bolted together, an irrigation pipe running straight through all four, and a drained third-depth bin in every cell. The checks found no errors and no mesh clashes. The bins are shallow because cells with the pipe through them only take third-depth bins. Caps on the open edges were left off; they are optional.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: 1 run IRRIGATION: non-potable supply. Corners are flexible hose, glued into Sch 40 sockets, one coupling wherever hose meets rigid pipe.

Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
